Created user_active_sessions with create.sql and rollback.sql: one active row per person per machine, the token held as a salted hash, with expiry, issued time and the machine key, giving 12 columns, 2 unique keys, 2 indexes and 2 foreign keys
Added the upsert, get, clear and list procedures for user_active_sessions, each with its rollback, and a validation script wired into the schema validator and the local installer's deploy list

Created auth_remembered_sign_ins with create.sql, rollback.sql, the read, upsert and clear procedures each with a rollback, and a validation script, keyed by person and machine and holding the encrypted payload, its initialisation vector and a key fingerprint

Extended ops_startup_logs with module, error_type, exception_detail and error_fingerprint plus the six panel indexes, by amending create.sql in place and extending rollback.sql with guarded per-object drops, which is the convention the existing table folders use; the first draft dropped the index before its foreign key and MySQL refused it with error 1553, corrected to key then index then column

Added sp_ops_startup_logs_insert as the single writer, taking the fingerprint as a parameter, taking a named lock before it reads so two writers cannot both link to the same predecessor, and reading, hashing and inserting inside one transaction; a writer that cannot take the lock within ten seconds is refused rather than guessing a predecessor

Added the panel reader sp_ops_startup_logs_filter with its filter set, grouping by error_fingerprint through sp_ops_startup_logs_fingerprint_groups_get, and sp_ops_startup_logs_purge bounded by age and by size, oldest first, each with its rollback; a deliberate race of two clients inserting eight entries each landed 16 rows with 0 broken links and every hash recomputing

Extended the startup schema validation with the four new columns, the six indexes and a non-null entry_hash; with the extension applied it reports 0 issues, and against the un-migrated store it reports exactly those 10 as missing, which is the assertion working rather than a defect

Found the specification premise wrong and fixed it: config_images_locations carried no computer scope, and its unique key is scope plus scope_item_id, so a machine row could exist for one machine only. Added a nullable computer_id with its foreign key and index and two procedures, and expressed the machine shape inside the item id as computer_id:source_kind rather than adding the nullable column to the unique key, which would have silently permitted duplicates because a UNIQUE key treats NULLs as distinct. No column was added to core_computers_registry

Added the four permission keys to the catalogue constants and the registry with their resource entries and strings, leaving permission.settings.ignored_locations exactly as it was, and corrected the one hard-coded settings-card permission count in a test the change invalidated

Verified rather than changed: the shipped development seed already assigns developer to johnk and jkoll, and the grant is person-scoped because auth_roles_assignments carries no machine column, so it holds on both seeded machines and needed no edit

Wrote the logging security review and recorded what it proves and what it cannot. Proved on the shipped artifacts: the log store has no credential column, exactly two statements touch it and neither is an update, the insert is the only writer and its parameter list cannot carry a secret, and neither trigger mentions the store. Could not prove: the seam, serializers and provider do not exist yet, so the prohibition holds because nothing writes rather than because code refuses

Registered tables 34 and 35 and the extended table 10 in the table aggregate, added their descriptions and the four new log columns to the descriptions file, and amended the config_images_locations block and its machine scope, which the ruleset requires and which omitting would have left wrong
Registered the thirteen new session, remembered-sign-in, log and machine-source procedures in the procedure aggregate, including the two T051 added that the previous unit left unregistered
Registered the amended seeds in the seed aggregate

Built the logging seam and its entry type unconditionally, with no Conditional attribute and no debug guard anywhere in the project so a release build records what a debug build records, and made the seam itself capture the machine, the person, the error type, the serialised exception chain and the derived fingerprint so no call site supplies or hashes anything

Built StoreLogWriter over a bounded channel in DropOldest mode, so a caller returns before the store is touched and a full queue discards its oldest entry rather than the newest fault, with the flush bounded at five seconds and a write that outlasted it cancelled; the writer takes no logger and no seam, so its own failure cannot produce a second diagnostic

Built StoreLoggerProvider as an ILoggerProvider so the 226 existing ILogger call sites across 26 files write to the same store with no call site edited: the category becomes the module, the level maps to severity and outcome, the exception goes through the seam's serializer, and structured state lands in payload_json rather than the message. MTM_Waitlist.Mock.Service builds its own container and is not served

Registered the writer as the host's hosted service so the shutdown flush is bounded, the seam behind ILogService as one shared instance, and the provider as an ILoggerProvider, and removed the last file-based registration, the StartupLoggingOptions Configure call in the app host, the earlier hosted and forwarder registrations having already gone with T008

Defined the step model as an immutable record of id, name, description, category, stated maximum wait and the best-effort marker, with no counting member on it at all, so the displayed count is derived from the catalog length and from the distinct steps the feed says have ended rather than being stored anywhere

Built the append-only activity feed carrying the timestamp, the step, the entry kind, the text, the target and the outcome; it is append-only structurally rather than by convention, because the only mutating member adds one entry under a lock, there is no clear remove or reorder member to call, the entries view is read-only and throws on an attempt to change it, and an entry has no setter

Built the runner so it appends the step's own name to the feed before the work starts, which is why an announcement survives a step that throws on its first statement, then races the step against its stated maximum and on overrun cancels it, observes the abandoned task so it cannot resurface, and records one failure naming the bound it passed; a blocking step fails with a retry remedy while a best-effort step is skipped so it cannot stop the launch, and a step declaring no maximum is refused rather than given an invented one

Built the step catalog as data: eleven steps with a stated maximum each, none unbounded and none past the thirty-second ceiling, and the picture refresh and external-system priming bounded well inside it as the two best-effort steps; the sequence is validated as it is built, so an unbounded step, an over-ceiling step, a best-effort step at the ceiling, a repeated id or a nameless step all fail immediately rather than shipping
